Neha / team — legal reviewed. High-level stance: we should avoid an unlimited carve-out. For SaaS agreements we typically:

1) Carve out death/personal injury and physical damage caused by a party's negligence from the general liability cap (this is a standard, narrow exception).
2) Avoid opening an exception for consequential or indirect damages.
3) If customer insists on a broader carve-out, require that it be limited to (i) direct physical injury or damage, (ii) caused by Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct, or (iii) covered by our commercial general liability (CGL) and tech E&O fleet insurance — whichever provides the clearer recovery path.

Suggested redline (proposed compromise):
"Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Agreement, neither Party's liability under this Agreement shall be limited to the extent such liability arises from death or personal injury caused by its negligence, or for damage to tangible property caused by its negligence. For clarity, this exception shall not apply to claims for economic loss, interruption of business, or other indirect or consequential damages. Subject to the foregoing, the aggregate liability cap set forth in Section X shall continue to apply to all other claims"

Further recommendations: request insurer name and COI showing limits (we typically carry X/X/X). If GreenGrid insists on unlimited liability for all physical damage (not tied to negligence), escalate to Legal Director (Jonas) + Sales leadership for approval — insurance/legal will need to assess risk and pricing.

I can prepare a redline .docx for Neha to send; recommend proposing the "negligence-limited" carve-out + COI. If GreenGrid presses for broader language, advise taking a pricing/underwriting approach rather than conceding contractually.

Marissa
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
